html:
The Wanggamala, also spelt Wangkamana and in many other ways, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the desert edge where Queensland meets the Northern Territory, on the map along the Mulligan River country.

This region was one source of pituri, a native tobacco plant chewed as a stimulant and traded across hundreds of kilometres. Their neighbours included the Pitta Pitta, Mithaka, Andegerebenha and Yarluyandi. Little else is recorded about them, and cattle stations took the better waters from the 1880s.
sum: The Wanggamala, also spelt Wangkamana and in many other ways, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the desert edge where Queensland meets the Northern Territory, on the map along the Mulligan River country.
